title: Almost-everywhere measurability of sections and parameter integrals
statement:
Use $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. Let $E$ be a separable real Banach space with its Borel measurable structure. A function is almost everywhere strongly measurable if, outside a null set, it is the pointwise limit of measurable simple functions; a simple function has finite image and measurable fibres. On any measure space $(Z,ho)$, an $E$-valued function equal almost everywhere to a measurable map is almost everywhere strongly measurable. An $E$-valued function measurable for the completion of $ho$ is equal $ho$-almost everywhere to a function measurable for the original sigma-algebra. Let $(X,\mu)$ and $(Y,
u)$ be sigma-finite measure spaces and let $H:X	imes Y	o E$ be almost everywhere strongly measurable for $\mu	imes
u$. Then $y\mapsto H(x,y)$ is almost everywhere strongly measurable for almost every $x$, and $$x\longmapsto\int_Y H(x,y)\,d
u(y)$$ is almost everywhere strongly measurable for $\mu$, with the Bochner integral set to zero on a nonintegrable section. Also, for every almost everywhere strongly measurable $v:Y	o E$, the map $(x,y)\mapsto v(y)$ is almost everywhere strongly measurable for $\mu	imes
u$.

AEStronglyMeasurable.prodMk_left at Integral/Prod.lean:148–153 gives sections; integral_prod_right' at 142–146 gives the parameter integral without global or sectionwise integrability hypotheses; comp_snd at 136–138 gives the lifted function. Sigma-finite measures supply SFinite. Complex Euclidean spaces and the finite-dimensional matrix space, regarded as real spaces, satisfy all target-space assumptions, including dimension zero. Completion clause: specialize MeasureTheory.NullMeasurable.aemeasurable at Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/AEMeasurable.lean:388–410 to the Borel measurable target E, whose sigma-algebra is countably generated. Measurability for the completion means preimages of measurable sets are null measurable, the definition of NullMeasurable. This is one direct specialization.
